name: 19506-batchdecode-kimilinear48b-tp4
model: moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct -- bf16, UNQUANTIZED, ungated on HF. ~49 B parameters, ~96 GB of safetensors, ~24 GB per card at TP4, ~3 B active per token. Not substitutable: no other public checkpoint serves this architecture at this scale.
hardware: 4x H100 80GB HBM3, NVLink, four cards of one a3 node. No router, no external cache tier, no second node.
parallelism: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism, no speculative decoding (the checkpoint ships no draft head).
architecture: KimiLinearForCausalLM, a 27-layer hybrid: 20 Kimi Delta Attention layers (linear, recurrent, a fixed-size state per request rather than a per-token cache) and 7 MLA layers, so KV is only ~8 KiB/token; sparse MoE, 256 routed experts at top-8 plus one shared expert; hidden_size 2304, vocab 163840, model_max_length 1048576.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=128, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 512 requests with an 1800 s safety cap -- four full waves, three of them measured.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix, streaming. 4096 prompt tokens against 768 output tokens, both FIXED with no spread, at `temperature: 0.0` with `ignore_eos: true`, so every request generates its full declared length and the running batch stays full throughout. Seed 42.
purpose: A long-context document analysis assistant streaming 1536-token answers to 128 concurrent users on four GPUs.
launch:
# The launch config, in `sglang serve` CLI form.

model-path: moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct
tp-size: 4

# Required by the checkpoint: its tokenizer_config.json sets
# auto_map.AutoTokenizer = ["tokenization_kimi.TikTokenTokenizer", null], so it is remote code.
trust-remote-code: true

random-seed: 42

# Everything else is a stock default of the pinned commit. Two that matter when reading a log:
#   - context-length unset means the checkpoint's own 1048576, which implies a ~8.6 GB per-rank
#     request-to-token table allocated OUTSIDE the mem-fraction-static budget. It is the first
#     place to look if a server OOMs at start-up; the lever is --mem-fraction-static, downward.
#   - sglang force-disables the radix cache for this architecture and says so in the log, so the
#     reported cache-hit rate is 0 by construction and is not a defect. The workload has no
#     shared prefix, and --disable-radix-cache is not passed because it would restate this.
